title: Protocol to prepare doubly labeled fluorescent nucleosomes for single-molecule fluorescence microscopy
protocol: Equilibrate fresh agar plates supplemented with Carben and CAM (or Carben only in case of H2B) to 22°C.
Mix 1 μL of plasmid with 50 μL chemically competent Rosetta 2 (DE3) pLysS cells (or BL21 (DE3) in case of H2B).
Incubate the plasmid-cells mixture on ice for 15 min.
Incubate the mixture at 42°C for 45 s.
Incubate the mixture back on ice for 5 min.
Incubate plasmid-cell mixture in 1 mL of LB media at 37°C for 30 minutes, shaking at 300 rpm.
Spread 100 μL of plasmid-cell-LB mixture on an agar plate.
Incubate the agar plate at 37°C for 16 hours.
Transfer 10 mL sterile 2×YT supplied with 10 μL Carben and 10 μL CAM (or Carben only in case of H2B) to each of 50 mL tubes.
Add 50 μL of 20% glucose to the tube.
Incubate these small cultures at 37°C, shaking at 220 rpm until slightly turbid.
Transfer 0.5 mL from each liquid culture to a sterile 1.5 mL tube.
Mix with 0.2 mL sterile 80% glycerol.
Store glycerol stocks at -80°C.
Induce expression by adding IPTG: for H2A, add 4 μL of 1 M IPTG stock; for H2B, add 2 μL; for H3, add 4 μL; and for H4, add 2 μL to each 10 mL liquid culture.
Keep one small culture without IPTG as an uninduced control.
Incubate small cultures at 37°C, shaking at 220 rpm for 4 hours.
Incubate small cultures at 37°C, shaking at 220 rpm for 2 hours.
Incubate small cultures at 37°C, shaking at 220 rpm for 3 hours.
Incubate small cultures at 52°C, shaking at 220 rpm for 3 hours.
Spin liquid cultures at 22°C for 20 minutes at 7,000 × g.
Discard supernatant after spinning the liquid cultures.
Store cell pellets at -20°C for analysis later.
Lysate the cell pellet by mixing with 500 μL MilliQ H2O and pipetting up and down for 3 minutes.
Mix 10 μL total cell lysate with 2 μL gel loading solution (6×).
Heat mixture at 95°C for 7 minutes.
Spin the mixture at 22°C for 6 minutes at 4,600 × g.
Load supernatants only on a 15% SDS-polyacrylamide gel.
Run samples on the gel at 120 V for 75 minutes.
Stain and image the gel to determine the best expressing colony.
Streak an agar plate with the glycerol stock of the best expressing colony.
Incubate the streaked agar plate at 37°C for 16 hours.
Transfer 4 mL 2×YT, 20 μL glucose, 4 μL Carben and 4 μL CAM to each of five sterile 50 mL tubes.
Inoculate each of the five tubes with a single colony from the same agar plate.
Incubate starter cultures shaking at 250 rpm until slightly turbid.
Incubate H2A for 16 hours at 21°C.
Inoculate the pre-culture with 4 starter cultures for H2A.
Incubate the pre-culture shaking at 220 rpm at 37°C until OD600 reaches 0.5 (∼ 5–6 h).
Transfer 100 mL of 2×YT to a sterile 500 mL flask.
Add 0.5 mL glucose, 100 μL Carben and 100 μL CAM (or Carben only in case of H2B) to the pre-culture media.
Keep aside 2 mL liquid media as blank solution for OD600 measurements.
Transfer 20 mL pre-culture to each 1 L liquid media for expression culture.
Incubate the cultures shaking at 220 rpm at 37°C until OD600 reaches 0.4-0.5 (∼ 3–4 h).
Add 5 mL glucose, 0.75 mL Carben and 0.75 mL CAM (or Carben only in case of H2B) to each sterile 3 L flask containing 1 L of 2×YT.
Incubate H2B for 2 hours at 37°C until OD600 reaches 0.1–0.2.
Inoculate the pre-culture with the most turbid starter culture for H2B.
Incubate H3 for approximately 1.5 hours at 37°C until OD600 reaches 0.4.
Inoculate the pre-culture with 2 starter cultures for H3.
Incubate H4 for approximately 2 hours at 37°C until OD600 reaches 0.4.
Inoculate the pre-culture with 4 starter cultures for H4.
Add IPTG at 0.4 mM to induce H2A expression in a 1 L liquid culture by adding 0.4 mL of 1 M IPTG stock.
Incubate the H2A culture at 37°C shaking at 220 rpm for 4 h.
Add IPTG at 0.2 mM to induce H2B expression in a 1 L liquid culture by adding 0.2 mL of 1 M IPTG stock.
Incubate the H2B culture at 37°C shaking at 220 rpm for 2 h.
Add IPTG at 0.4 mM to induce H3 expression in a 1 L liquid culture by adding 0.4 mL of 1 M IPTG stock.
Incubate the H3 culture at 37°C shaking at 220 rpm for 3 h.
Add IPTG at 0.2 mM to induce H4 expression in a 1 L liquid culture by adding 0.2 mL of 1 M IPTG stock.
Incubate the H4 culture at 37°C shaking at 220 rpm for 3 h.
Keep aside 10 mL from each 1 L liquid culture to test expression using SDS-PAGE before proceeding with extraction of inclusion bodies and purification.
Spin cultures at 6,000 rpm for 30 min at 4°C.
Thoroughly resuspend the cell pellet from each 1 L culture in 30 mL 2×YT by pipetting and vortexing.
Transfer the suspension to a sterile 50 mL tube and spin for 30 min at 7,000 × g at 4°C.
Discard supernatant.
Store pellets at -20°C (for weeks) or at -80°C (for months).
Resuspend pellet from 1 L liquid bacterial culture in 20 mL histone lysis buffer by pipetting and vortexing thoroughly.
Do four freeze/thaw cycles using dry ice and a 37°C water bath.
Stir the cell suspension for 20 minutes with a magnetic stirrer in a beaker.
Add Triton X-100 to the cell resuspension (1% or 0.2 mL in 20 mL lysis buffer).
Stir for an additional 10 minutes.
Transfer the mixture to a stainless-steel beaker.
Perform sonication with 10 cycles of 10 seconds ON and 30 seconds OFF at an amplitude of 400 Watts power and a frequency of 20 kHz, keeping the beaker on ice throughout the process.
Spin the cell lysate at 7,000 × g for 40 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in histone lysis buffer supplemented with 1% Triton x-100 (20 mL per 1 L of pellet).
Spin at 7,000 × g for 30 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Repeat steps 22 to 24.
Resuspend the pellet in buffer without Triton (20 mL per 1 L of pellet).
Spin at 7,000 × g for 30 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Add 500 μL of DMSO to the pellet and break it up well with a spatula.
Let sit at 22°C for 30 minutes.
Slowly add histone Gdn-HCl buffer (10 mL per 1 L cell pellet).
Mix with a spatula and transfer to a beaker.
Stir for 1 hour at 22°C.
Spin at 7,000 × g for 30 minutes.
Save the supernatant, which contains the solubilized histone.
Re-extract the pellet from step 36 by repeating steps 30 to 36.
Keep 20–30 μL sample before dialysis to check for protein expression by SDS-PAGE.
Prepare 2.5 L of 8 M urea.
Add 50 g mixed ion exchange resin and stir for 1 h.
Dialyze 20 mL histone extract into 2.5 L of 8 M urea at 22°C for 16 h.
Recover histone extract from dialysis cassette.
Keep aside 50 μL sample from the dialysis products for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Remove beads of mixed ion exchange resin from the 8 M urea solution using a bottle-top filter.
Pre-equilibrate 5 mL Q-Sepharose into 8 M urea as follows: Pour Q-Sepharose resin into a clean glass gravity column and let it settle.
Drain storage solution from Q-Sepharose.
Wash with 6 CV of MilliQ H2O before mixing with urea (30 mL total).
Wash with 3 CV of 8 M urea (15 mL total).
Incubate the dialyzed histone extract with pre-equilibrated Q-Sepharose resin for 1 h while rocking.
Collect flow-through from the column.
Wash the column with an additional 6 CV (30 mL) of 8 M urea.
Keep the wash.
Pre-equilibrate 25 mL SP-Sepharose into 8 M urea by pouring resin into a clean glass gravity column, draining storage solution, washing with 6 CV (150 mL) of MilliQ H2O and then 3 CV of 8 M urea.
Mix the first flow-through from the Q-sepharose with the pre-equilibrated SP-Sepharose.
Incubate this mixture for 2 h while rocking.
Discard the flow-through after incubation.
Run the wash from Q-sepharose over SP-Sepharose and discard the flow-through.
Wash with an additional 2 CV of 8 M urea.
Elute with a step gradient of NaCl by pouring 30 mL of each solution in steps: 200 mM, 300 mM, 400 mM, 500 mM, 600 mM, and 700 mM NaCl in 8 M urea.
Save the flow-through fraction of each gradient step.
Prepare a 15% (29:1) SDS polyacrylamide gel with dimensions of 7 × 8 × 0.15 cm (W × H × D), containing 15 wells and 40 μL well volume.
Mix 10 μL of each fraction with gel loading solution then load on the gel.
Run samples at 120 V for 75 minutes in the presence of 1× Tris/glycine/SDS gel running buffer.
Stain the gel according to instructions from the stain manufacturer.
Destain the gel following the manufacturer's instructions.
Pool fractions containing the target protein.
Dialyze fractions containing histones into 2.5 L MilliQ H2O supplemented with 2 mM BME (0.35 mL of 14 M stock).
Use a 3.5 kDa MWCO dialysis cassette for histones, larger than the total volume of fractions due to volume increase post-dialysis.
Change dialysis water for a total of 5 times, with at least two steps running for 16 hours each.
Add BME during each change of dialysis solution.
Remove particles from the histone solution by spinning at 7,000 × g for 10 minutes.
Clean centrifugal filters (3.5 kDa MWCO) with dialysis solution and discard any remaining solution after spinning at 5,000 × g for 10 minutes.
Concentrate the histone solution 12-fold.
Filter undissolved particles from the concentrated histone solution using a 0.22 μm syringe filter.
Set aside approximately 50 μL of the final histone solution.
Measure the concentration of the histone solution at 280 nm using the molar absorption coefficient for each specific histone.
Check quality of purified histone using 15% (29:1) SDS-PAGE.
Flash freeze the concentrated histone solution in 50 mL conical tubes then lyophilize.
Resuspend a portion of the lyophilized histone in MilliQ H2O with concentration and volume according to the instructions of the mass spectroscopy facility.
Label human H2A K119C containing a single Cysteine residue with Cy3.5 maleimide under denaturing conditions.
Reconstitute histone and fluorescent dye under minimal light.
Equilibrate lyophilized histone and fluorescent dye to 22°C for approximately 1 hour in the dark.
Weigh 1 mg of histone into an autoclaved microcentrifuge tube.
Mix the weighed histone with 800 μL labeling buffer to achieve a concentration of approximately 90 μM.
Add 2 μL of 0.5 M TCEP to stabilize free sulfhydryls in the mixture (final concentration is 1.25 mM).
Incubate the mixture for 2 hours at 22°C while mixing using a tube revolver.
Measure the absorbance at 280 nm (A280) of the histone mixture and determine its concentration.
Set aside 15 μL of the histone solution for analysis with SDS-PAGE as a reference sample.
Mix 1 mg of Cy3.5 maleimide with 26.5 μL DMSO by slowly pipetting up and down in the dark.
Transfer all of the dye solution to the histone solution (total volume approximately 828.5 μL) leading to a dye excess over histone of about 11 times molar ratio (∼ 87 μM histone and ∼ 1 mM dye).
Incubate the mixture for 16 hours at 4°C in the dark while mixing using tube revolver.
Further incubate the mixture at 22°C for 1.5 hours.
Do all the work of this procedure at 22°C.
Wash each centrifugal filter with labeling buffer.
Spin filters at 12,000 × g for 5 minutes.
Reverse spin filters at 21,000 × g for a few seconds.
Stop the labeling reaction by adding ∼5 μL of BME.
Keep aside 15 μL sample for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Transfer half of the crude fluorescent histone solution to each centrifugal filter.
Spin at 12,000 × g for 45 minutes.
Transfer filters with the histone solution to two new tubes.
Fill each filter with fresh labeling buffer containing 7 M Gdn-HCl.
Reverse spin for 10 seconds at 21,000 × g to recover labeled histone.
Wash two new centrifugal filters as in previous steps.
Split the labeled histone solution into the two new filters.
Spin until volume is reduced to a third of original volume (≤ 30 minutes).
Repeat removing excess dyes with a third pair of new filters (i.e., total three rounds of spinning each with a new pair of filters).
Spin at 12,000 × g until the total volume in both filters is reduced to 120 μL.
Keep aside 5 μL of purified labeled histone for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Aliquot the purified fluorescent into 20 μL aliquots.
Flash freeze and store at -80°C.
Prepare a 15% (29:1) SDS-polyacrylamide gel with dimensions 7 × 8 × 0.15 cm (W × H × D).
Load unlabeled histone sample from step 80 for reference determination of total mass loaded per well of the purified labeled histone sample.
Run crude labeled histone before removing excess dye on SDS gel.
Run purified labeled histone after removing excess dye on SDS gel.
Calculate concentrations and dilutions to load ≥ 5 μg histone per well.
Load 50 μL per well for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Dilute purified labeled histone by mixing 1 μL sample with 6 μL MilliQ H2O.
Mix 5 μL of diluted or undiluted labeled histone, 8.33 μL gel loading solution (6×), and 36.66 μL MilliQ H2O for each sample to be loaded per well.
Heat the samples at 95°C for 5 min before loading on the SDS gel.
Run samples on the SDS gel covered from light at 120 V for 1 hour and 45 minutes or until free dye reaches the bottom of the gel.
Carry out fluorescence imaging of the gel while it is still between the glass plates.
Take the gel off the glass plates.
Stain and destain the gel according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Image the gel using default Coomassie stain settings.
Analyze the gel image using ImageJ or any equivalent software.
Find the net integrated intensity of the reference band by subtracting background.
Find the net integrated intensity of the purified labeled histone band in the same way.
Calculate the ratio of the net integrated intensities of purified labeled over unlabeled histone bands.
Calculate the total reference mass loaded on gel (Mref) using the concentration of the reference unlabeled histone solution and its volume.
Calculate the total mass of labeled histone (ML) loaded on gel as ML = RLU × Mref.
Calculate the concentration of labeled histone (μg/μL) as 7 × (ML/VL), where VL is the volume of 7×-diluted purified labeled histone.
Resuspend 5′-amino-modified ssDNA primers in autoclaved 10 mM Tris-Cl (pH 8) to a final concentration of 100 μM.
Cool 50 mL ethanol on ice for 1 hour.
Mix 2 mL DNA solution, 0.2 mL sodium acetate (3M, pH 5.2), and 6.6 mL cold ethanol.
Incubate the mixture at −80°C for 40 minutes.
Spin down the precipitate at 7,000 × g for 25 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to another tube.
Resuspend the pellet from the first precipitation in 2 mL of 10 mM Tris-Cl (pH 8).
Add sodium acetate and ethanol to the resuspended pellet.
Incubate at −80°C.
Spin at 16,000 × g for 15 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet from the second precipitation in 2 mL of 10 mM Tris-Cl (pH 8).
Add sodium acetate and ethanol as in the first precipitation.
Split the 8.8 mL solution into 10 aliquots, each containing 880 μL.
Incubate each aliquot at −80°C for 40 min.
Spin each aliquot at 16,000 × g for 15 min at 4°C.
Rinse the pellet three times by adding and removing 1 mL of ice cold ethanol without disrupting the pellet.
Dry the pellets for 1 hour on a bench with the caps open.
Resuspend one of the pellets in 10 μL DNAse-free H2O.
Transfer this resuspension to the second microcentrifuge tube.
Repeat the resuspension process until all pellets are combined into one tube, using 100 μL of DNAse-free H2O total.
Dilute 1 μL of the cleaned primer so that the absorbance at 260 nm (A260) is below 1 for a 1 cm pathlength.
Prepare dye stock solution by resuspending each 1 mg in 9.5 μL DMSO (final concentration 80 mM for Cy5.5 NHS ester).
Prepare primer working stock solution by mixing 10 μL of a 1 mM stock with 10 μL DNAse-free H2O (final concentration 0.5 mM).
Assemble each labeling reaction in sterile microcentrifuge tubes.
Incubate at 30°C for 16 hours shaking at 700 rpm in a thermomixer.
Mix each 20 μL labeling reaction with 2 μL NaCl (3M) and 50 μL ethanol.
Incubate at −20°C for 5 hours.
Spin at 12,000 × g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Discard supernatant.
Rinse each pellet three times with 1 mL ice cold ethanol.
Spin at 12,000 × g for 2 minutes at 4°C then remove the supernatant.
Dry pellets for 1 hour by opening the cap of each microcentrifuge tube and leaving it on its side inside a dark cabinet.
Resuspend the pellet of each reaction/tube in 20 μL of autoclaved 10 mM Tris-Cl (pH 8).
Combine all resuspended reactions in one tube.
Optimize PCR reaction conditions on a small-scale before carrying out hundreds of 50 μL-PCR reactions.
Prepare a single 50 μL PCR reaction according to the optimized conditions.
Assemble 5 mL PCR mixture for 100 PCR reactions.
Mix 1 mL of Phusion HF buffer (5×) into the assembly.
Add 100 μL of template DNA solution with a concentration of 10 ng/μL.
Combine 100 μL of dNTPs mix with a concentration of 10 mM each dNTP.
Mix 250 μL of forward fluorescent primer diluted to 10 μM based on the stock concentration.
Resuspend reverse biotin-labeled primer in autoclaved 10 mM Tris-Cl (pH 8) at 100 μM solution.
Determine accurate concentration of biotin-labeled primer by measuring absorbance at 260 nm.
Prepare 250 μL of reverse primer diluted to 10 μM concentration.
Reconstitute Phusion DNA polymerase according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Transfer 3.2 mL DNAse-free H2O to a sterile 15 mL tube.
Mix the transferred water with all total amounts shown in step 141.
Distribute 5 mL PCR reaction mixture over 100 PCR tubes on ice.
Run the PCR reaction using specified settings.
Pool all 100 PCR reactions back into one sterile 15 mL tube.
Wrap pooled reactions with aluminum foil to protect from light.
Set aside 20 μL for checking yield with agarose gel electrophoresis.
Store remaining PCR products at −20°C until purification time or proceed immediately with purification.
Prepare a 1.5% agarose gel (7 × 7 cm) supplied with Sybr Safe stain diluted 1:5000.
Load 10 μL per well of the crude PCR products.
Load 10 μL of 100-bp DNA ladder per well.
Thaw on ice the 5 mL PCR pool if stored at -20°C.
Cool 50 mL of 100% ethanol on ice for 1 hour.
Mix the PCR pool with 0.5 mL sodium acetate (3 M, pH 5.2) and 13.75 mL ice-cold 100% ethanol.
Incubate the mixture for 16 hours at -20°C in the dark.
Spin the mixture for 30 minutes at 7,200 × g at 4°C.
Discard supernatant.
Cool 50 mL of 70% ethanol on ice for 1 hour.
Slowly add 20 mL of 70% ethanol without disrupting the pellet.
Spin the mixture for 30 minutes at 7,200 × g at 4°C.
Discard supernatant.
Air dry the pellet by opening the cap and leaving it on its side inside a dark cabinet for 3 hours.
Resuspend the dried pellet in 500 μL of T50 buffer.
Incubate at 37°C for 10 minutes if resuspension is difficult.
Store T50 buffer stock at 22°C.
Prepare a 5% non-denaturing polyacrylamide gel with dimensions of 20 × 16 × 0.3 cm and well dimensions of 2.7 × 2.3 × 0.3 cm.
Prepare 4 L of 0.5× TBE buffer by mixing 3.8 L MilliQ H2O with 0.2 L of 10× TBE.
Filter the 10× TBE with a 0.22 μm bottle top filter into an autoclaved bottle and store at 22°C.
Move all tools and reagents to a cold room (4°C) and equilibrate for at least 1 hour.
Pre-run the gel for 1 hour at 5 V/cm (100 V total for 20 cm long gel).
Thaw the DNA sample if frozen.
Spin the DNA sample with 14,000 × g for 15 minutes at 22°C to remove insoluble proteins.
Mix 55.6 μL glycerol with 500 μL DNA sample (final 10% v/v glycerol concentration).
Rinse the gel wells three times with fresh 0.5× TBE buffer.
Load all samples in one well using a 1 mL Luer syringe attached to an 18 Gauge needle.
Run the sample on the gel at 5 V/cm (100 V total for 20 cm long gel) in a cold room (4°C) for 3 hours.
Clean a new razor with MilliQ H2O and 70% ethanol.
Take the gel off the glass plates and place it on Saran wrap plastic.
Do not excise the gel band while the gel is on the glass plate.
Excise the band with a razor.
Move the gel slice to a sterile 15 mL tube.
Store the gel slices at −20°C or proceed to the next step.
Soak gel slices in 5 mL of autoclaved 10 mM Tris-Cl (pH 7.5) buffer.
Incubate for 16 h at 37°C with shaking (or rotating).
Keep the supernatant, which contains DNA that diffused out of the gel slices.
Crush the gel slices using a sterile 1 mL pipette tip.
Repeat soaking in fresh 5 mL buffer, incubating for 16 h at 37°C.
Combine the supernatants from both rounds of soaking (total volume is 10 mL).
Filter supernatant to remove gel particles using a 20 mL Luer syringe fit to a 0.22 μm syringe filter.
Add an equal volume of 2-butanol to the combined supernatants.
Mix well and spin at 7,000 × g for 1 min at 4°C.
Discard the upper organic layer.
Repeat the 2-butanol extraction until the volume of aqueous phase is less than or equal to 500 μL.
In the last round, discard the upper layer, spin again without adding butanol, then remove traces of butanol from the top of the aqueous DNA solution.
Measure the exact volume of the extracted aqueous fluorescent DNA solution.
Cool 10 mL of 100% ethanol on ice for at least 30 min.
Mix the fluorescent DNA sample with 50 μL sodium acetate (3 M, pH 5.2).
Add 2.5× volume cold 100% ethanol to the mixture.
Incubate for 16 hours at -20°C in the dark.
Spin the mixture for 15 minutes at 15,000 × g at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Rinse the pellet by adding 1.5 mL ice cold 100% ethanol.
Incubate the mixture at 15,000 × g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Pipette out the ethanol without disrupting the pellet.
Air dry the pellet for 1 hour on its side inside a dark cabinet.
Resuspend the dried pellet in 25 μL autoclaved TE buffer.
Do not freeze the resuspended pellet.
Use a set of online calculators to estimate different values of ɛ260 for a specific DNA sequence.
Calculate the concentration using the mean of all estimated ɛ260 values.
Dilute 2 μL of purified fluorescent DNA solution 80× using resuspension buffer.
Blank the spectrophotometer with the same buffer used for resuspension and dilution.
Measure the absorbance at 260 nm (A260) of the diluted DNA solution.
If A260 is >1, further dilute the DNA solution and repeat measuring A260.
Concentration of DNA using the formula [DNA] = (A260 / (ε260 × 1 cm)) × DF.
Ignore dye absorption at 260 nm due to its small coefficient compared to DNA and minor correction factor.
Run purified fluorescent dsDNA on a 7 x 8 cm non-denaturing PAGE for quality assessment.
Refold fluorescent octamer over a period of 5 days.
Equilibrate the unlabeled lyophilized frozen histones to 22°C.
Thaw the fluorescent histone stock on ice.
Weigh ∼ 2 mg of each of the unlabeled histones into separate autoclaved microcentrifuge tubes.
Dissolve each histone in 1 ml of unfolding buffer rotating for 1 h at 22°C using tube revolver.
Measure the absorbances at 280 nm (A280) to determine the exact concentrations of all unlabeled histones.
Determine the volumes of H2A and H2B solutions that contain 40.2 nmol based on calculated concentrations.
Determine the volumes of H3 and H4 solutions that contain 33.5 nmol based on calculated concentrations.
Combine solutions of all 4 histones to a total volume less than 1 mL.
Dilute the combined histone solutions with unfolding buffer to a final volume of 2 mL.
Equilibrate 250 mL of refolding buffer for 2 h in the cold room (4°C).
Add BME to the refolding buffer just before use.
Inject the sample into a 3-mL dialysis cassette (7 kDa MWCO) according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Dialyze for 16 h in 250 mL refolding buffer (125× dilution) at 4°C while stirring.
Wrap the beaker with aluminum foil, to protect the fluorescent dye from light.
Change buffer then repeat dialysis for 6–8 hours.
Change buffer a third time then repeat dialysis for another 16 hours.
Transfer the dialysate to an autoclaved tube and measure its volume.
Keep aside 10 μL for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Pellet down any aggregates by spinning at 18,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer supernatant to a new autoclaved microcentrifuge tube.
Concentrate the dialysate to reduce its volume to ≤ 500 μL.
Wash two centrifugal filters with refolding buffer.
Spin at 13,000 × g for 2 minutes at 4°C.
Remove buffer by inverting filters and pulse spinning.
Split dialysate into two equal parts.
Concentrate the first half of dialysate using two filters.
Spin to reduce volume in each filter to approximately 100 μL.
Transfer filters to new tubes.
Recover concentrated dialysate by inverting filters and spinning for 30 seconds at 6,500 × g.
Concentrate the second half of dialysate as above.
Collect a total of 400–500 μL of concentrated dialysate.
Set aside 5 μL for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Keep the remaining concentrated dialysate on ice until time of SEC.
If stored overnight, store dialysate on ice inside a 4°C refrigerator.
Purify the octamer over SEC using a Superdex 200 Increase 10/300 GL, or equivalent.
Adjust the volume of the concentrated dialysate to exactly 500 μL using SEC buffer.
Wash a 0.5 mL sample injection loop with 5 mL SEC buffer.
Inject sample into the loop.
Turn off light around machine or cover fraction collection module with dim cover.
Elute sample using a flow rate of 0.5 mL/min and collect 0.5 mL-fractions.
Transfer fractions of both elution peaks to autoclaved microcentrifuge tubes.
Store fractions on ice.
Chill centrifugal filters on ice for 15 minutes.
Clean the centrifugal filters by filling them with SEC buffer and spinning at 12,000 × g for 1 minute at 4°C.
Discard the buffer after cleaning.
Transfer elution fractions to the centrifugal filters.
Spin the filters at 12,000 × g for 7 minutes at 4°C until volume of each fraction is approximately 75 μL.
Measure A280 of the concentrated fractions of elution peaks.
Prepare an 18% (29:1) SDS-polyacrylamide gel with dimensions 7 × 8 × 0.15 cm (W × H × D).
Note: For best results, prepare a 10-well gel with well dimensions of 0.5 × 1 × 0.15 cm (W × H × D) and volume of 65 μL.
Calculate the concentration of octamer in the central fraction of the main elution peak using molar absorption coefficient at 280 nm (ɛ280) of 44,700 M-1cm-1.
Determine the volume to load of each of the fractions of the main elution peak.
Calculate the sample volume that contains 14 μg octamer (i.e., 3.5 μg of each histone).
If the concentration of the central fraction is 57 μM, then 2.28 μL will contain 14 μg octamer using an octamer M.W. of 108.42 kDa.
Load the same volume for the rest of the fractions of the main elution peak.
Calculate the ratio between A280 of the central fraction of the main elution peak and the central fraction of the secondary elution peak (scaling factor, SF).
For fraction at the center of the secondary elution peak, load a sample volume equal to SF × volume of sample taken from the central fraction of the main elution peak.
Load the same sample volume for the rest of the fractions of the secondary elusion peak.
Dilute each sample 2× with MilliQ H2O.
Mix with gel loading solution.
Load all of the diluted sample in each well.
Run samples at 180 V for 110 min in 1× Tris/glycine/SDS gel running buffer.
Stain according to manufacturer’s instructions of protein stain.
Destain according to manufacturer’s instructions of protein stain.
Image the gel using default settings for Coomassie Brilliant Blue stain.
Mix slowly by pipetting to pool fractions that display equimolar quantities of all four histones.
Spin the pool at 1,000 × g for 1 min at 4°C.
Check for aggregation or phase separation.
Determine the concentration by measuring A280 and using the octamer ε280 mentioned above.
Blank with SEC buffer.
If needed, concentrate to ∼ 20 μM.
Store purified octamer on ice at 4°C for short-term storage (a few days to a couple of weeks).
Renew ice daily for short-term storage.
Store purified octamer long-term by freezing at -20°C with 50% glycerol.
Remove glycerol from stored octamer by dialysis into high salt buffer before use.
Repeat size exclusion chromatography (SEC) after removing glycerol.
Reconstitute nucleosome using a 1.25:1.0 molar ratio of DNA: octamer.
Dialyze the reconstituted nucleosome into buffer without salt by double dialysis.
Separate properly reconstituted nucleosomes from free DNA and other by-products by sucrose gradient.
Calculate the volume of fluorescent DNA solution containing 350 pmol based on stock concentration.
Calculate the volume of fluorescent octamer containing 280 pmol.
Combine DNA with a volume of 3 M NaCl solution to reach a final concentration of 2 M NaCl.
Add high salt buffer to bring the final volume to 200 μL.
Prepare high salt buffer using sterile tools and autoclaved MilliQ H2O, Tris-Cl, and EDTA stocks.
Filter the buffer with a 0.22 μm bottle top filter.
Store the buffer at 4°C.
Add benzamidine to the high salt buffer at time of use.
Add octamer as the last component to the mixture.
Keep the DNA-octamer mixture on ice until dialysis setup is ready.
Cool down no-salt buffers to 4°C for a couple of hours before use.
Prepare no-salt buffer using sterile tools and autoclaved MilliQ H2O, Tris-Cl, and EDTA stocks.
Filter the no-salt buffer with a 0.22 μm bottle top filter.
Store the buffer at 4°C.
Add benzamidine to the no-salt buffer on time of use.
Cut 20 cm of dialysis tubing (8 kDa MWCO and 5 cm flat width).
Immerse dialysis tubing in 1 L MilliQ H2O for 2 min, repeat two more times.
Move the dialysis tubing to 4 L no-salt buffer leaving one end open.
Fill the dialysis tubing with 50 mL high salt buffer.
Prevent the dialysis tubing from sinking into the 4 L no-salt buffer by anchoring.
Hydrate two mini dialysis devices (7 kDa MWCO, 100 μL capacity each) in 100 mL MilliQ H2O for 2 min.
Fill the hydrated mini dialysis devices with the DNA-octamer mixture.
Put the two mini dialysis devices into the larger dialysis tubing.
Close the larger dialysis tubing.
Attach the dialysis tubing to a floating buoy.
Dialyze at 4°C for 16 hours while slowly stirring in darkness.
Change dialysis buffer with 4 L of fresh no-salt buffer.
Dialyze for another 8 hours.
Change dialysis buffer again with 4 L of fresh no-salt buffer.
Let go for 16 hours.
Transfer the dialysate to an autoclaved microcentrifuge tube.
Store the dialysate on ice at 4°C until loading on sucrose gradient.
Keep aside 5 μL of dialysate for non-denaturing PAGE analysis.
Heat shock the dialysate at 37°C for 1 hour.
Cool the dialysate on ice after heat shocking.
Equilibrate all solutions and tools used for making sucrose gradient to 22°C.
Equilibrate ultracentrifuge, SW41 rotor, and buckets to 4°C.
Wash the ultracentrifuge tubes with autoclaved H2O.
Wash the ultracentrifuge tubes with 20% ethanol.
Wash the ultracentrifuge tubes with autoclaved MilliQ H2O.
Prepare a 5%-40% sucrose gradient.
Cool the sucrose gradient at 4°C for 1 hour.
Load all dialysate sample (∼200 μL) on the sucrose gradient in one ultracentrifuge tube.
Spin the ultracentrifuge tubes at 41,000 rpm for 22 hours at 4°C.
Collect 32 fractions of 0.35 mL each from the ultracentrifuge tube.
Clean a set of centrifugal filters using autoclaved 0.5× TE buffer according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Concentrate fractions of gradient until each fraction volume is ∼35 μL.
Spin for 90 min with 14,000 × g then collect concentrate.
Store concentrated fractions on ice in a 4°C fridge.
Dilute each concentrated fraction as necessary so that A260 is not > 1 using 0.5× TE buffer.
Measure the A260 of the fractions.
Blank using 0.5× TE buffer.
Wash the glass plates, spacers and comb with soap and warm water then dry them.
Rinse all components with ethanol 70% then wipe dry.
Prepare a 7 × 8 × 0.15 cm (W × H × D) non-denaturing polyacrylamide 5% (59:1) gel.
Cool electrophoresis device, gel, and buffer inside a cold room (4°C) for 1 h.
Pre-run the gel for 1 h at 125 V.
Dilute sample of each fraction with 0.5× TE so that the total volume is 5 μL.
Mix the 5 μL of each fraction with equal volume of non-denaturing gel loading solution (2×).
Rinse wells of the gel with fresh buffer.
Load samples onto the gel.
Cover electrophoresis tank to protect fluorescent dyes from light.
Run samples on gel at 125 V for 75 min.
Prepare 100 mL of 5 ng/mL EtBr solution in MilliQ H2O.
Take the gel off the glass plates.
Stain the gel for 15 min at 22°C while shaking.
Rinse once with MilliQ H2O without destaining.
Image the gel.
Pool fractions containing nucleosomes only.
Chill 50 mL of 1× TE on ice for ∼ 1 h before mixing with nucleosomes.
Clean a pair of centrifugal filters according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Transfer the nucleosome pool to a centrifugal filter.
Fill the filter with TE (1×).
Spin at 14,000 × g for 30 min.
Refill the filter and repeat spinning until volume is ∼ 35 μL.
Repeat spinning three times in total.
Recover the concentrate by inverting the filter inside a new tube.
Spin with 1,000 × g for 2 min.
Store nucleosomes and flow-through solutions in autoclaved microcentrifuge tubes at 4°C in darkness.
Measure A260 and calculate concentration after pooling and concentrating fractions.
Blank the measurement with 1× TE.
